## Setup
```{r}
pharma <- read.csv("Pharmaceuticals.csv")
str(pharma)

#vars 1-9 for clustering
numVars <- c("Market_Cap", "Beta", "PE_Ratio", "ROE", "ROA",
             "Asset_Turnover", "Leverage", "Rev_Growth", "Net_Profit_Margin")
catVars <- c("Median_Recommendation", "Location", "Exchange")

pharmaNum <- pharma[, numVars]
rownames(pharmaNum) <- pharma$Symbol #tickers as row names so plots show firm labels

summary(pharmaNum)
colSums(is.na(pharmaNum)) #no missing
```

## a. Clustering the 21 firms

### Normalize
```{r}
#euclidean distance is scale dependent, market cap (0.41 to 199) would drown out beta (0.18 to 1.11)
#z-score: subtract mean, divide by sd
pharmaNorm <- scale(pharmaNum)
round(head(pharmaNorm), 2)
```

### Weights
```{r}
#check correlation before deciding on weights
round(cor(pharmaNum), 2)
```

### Distance + outliers
```{r}
distance <- get_dist(pharmaNorm)
fviz_dist(distance)

#any firm more than 3 sd from the mean on a var
maxZ <- apply(abs(pharmaNorm), 1, max)
round(pharmaNorm[maxZ > 3, ], 2)
```

### Choosing k
```{r}
set.seed(123)
fviz_nbclust(pharmaNorm, kmeans, method = "wss", k.max = 10, nstart = 25)

set.seed(123)
fviz_nbclust(pharmaNorm, kmeans, method = "silhouette", k.max = 10, nstart = 25)
```

```{r}
#same checks as the plots in one table, plus smallest cluster size
kStats <- function(k, data) {
  set.seed(123)
  km <- kmeans(data, centers = k, nstart = 25)
  sil <- cluster::silhouette(km$cluster, dist(data))
  c(k = k,
    wss = round(km$tot.withinss, 1),
    betweenTotal = round(km$betweenss / km$totss, 3), #share of variation between clusters
    avgSil = round(mean(sil[, "sil_width"]), 3),
    smallest = min(km$size))
}

kTable <- as.data.frame(t(sapply(2:8, kStats, data = pharmaNorm)))
kTable
```

### Final model
```{r}
bestK <- 3

set.seed(123)
kmFinal <- kmeans(pharmaNorm, centers = bestK, nstart = 25) #25 random starts, keeps lowest wss
kmFinal$size
round(kmFinal$centers, 2)

fviz_cluster(kmFinal, data = pharmaNorm, repel = TRUE, ggtheme = ggplot2::theme_minimal())
```

### Stability + quality
```{r}
#kmeans is stochastic, rerun w/ 50 seeds to see if same solution comes back
runSeed <- function(seed, data, k) {
  set.seed(seed)
  round(kmeans(data, centers = k, nstart = 25)$tot.withinss, 2)
}
seedWss <- sapply(1:50, runSeed, data = pharmaNorm, k = bestK)
table(seedWss) #all 50 the same = stable

#silhouette per firm
silFinal <- cluster::silhouette(kmFinal$cluster, dist(pharmaNorm))
fviz_silhouette(silFinal, print.summary = FALSE)
round(tapply(silFinal[, "sil_width"], kmFinal$cluster, mean), 3) #avg per cluster

#separation: distance between centroids vs avg distance of firms to their own centroid
round(dist(kmFinal$centers), 2)
round(sqrt(kmFinal$withinss / kmFinal$size), 2)
```

### Manhattan distance check (flexclust)
```{r}
#same k, manhattan distance + median centroids (lecture: kcca w/ kmedians)
#kcca has no nstart, so run 25 seeds and keep the one w/ the lowest total distance
runKmed <- function(seed, data, k) {
  set.seed(seed)
  kcca(data, k = k, family = kccaFamily("kmedians"))
}
kmedRuns <- lapply(1:25, runKmed, data = pharmaNorm, k = bestK)
kmedDist <- sapply(kmedRuns, info, "distsum")
round(kmedDist, 2) #spread here = how much the start matters

kmMed <- kmedRuns[[which.min(kmedDist)]]
kmMed

#apply the predict() function, no new data = clusters of the original firms
medClusters <- predict(kmMed)
split(rownames(pharmaNorm), medClusters)

#compare to kmeans. rows = kmeans cluster, cols = kmedians cluster
compTable <- table(kmeans = kmFinal$cluster, kmedians = medClusters)
compTable
randIndex(compTable) #adjusted rand: 1 = same grouping, 0 = no better than chance
```

## Part A - Reasoning

```
Weights were left the same - no mention was made of these values holding more or less
importance than any other values. 
Z-score was used to normalize the scale since Euclidean distance is scale dependent.
Market cap would have otherwise decided everything.
Though weights weren't added manually, Euclidean distance ignores correlation, so
size/profitability end up acting as though they have a higher weight. 
ROE, ROA, Market Cap seem very correlated from the data/process used here.
I also ran Manhatten distance (following our class lectures) since this is supposed
to be better for when values are correlated - keeping the same lack of weights. 
Size&Profitability would be the main ways these are determined anyway.
Algo: kmeans w/ Euclidean distance; the 9 vars are all continuious numbers, with
the goal being to split firms into non overlapping groups (thus why we used kmeans)
nstart=25 (from slides, but runs 25 times from random starts) with static seed set.
Also ran against 50 other seeds to verify the result would be the same (for thoroughness)
Manhattan distance showed the 11 major firms came out the same, with 3 minor ones moving.
I maintained Euclidean distance for the assignment since it's more stable.
Outliers: Allergan, Chatterm
Both are >3 SD from mean on any vars.
I chose K=3 for my clustering because the silhouette peaks at k=3, and the elbow
plot had the larger drops between 1-2 and 2-3. K=2 would have been too small to have
meaningful clusters, so I went with 3. I also tried running this with k=5, but some
of the groups weren't visually meaningful, so I kept k=3 to maintain the clarity.
Our data set is rather small, so this made sense to me. More technically, I would
say that k=5 made the clusters weaker, and also to note; they fell apart under manhattan.
Quality: Avg silhouette .280; clusters are separated but not too sharply. This made
sense with our 21 firm & no obvious data gabs. Loosest cluster was AGN-AHM-BAY-PHA (.136)
and AHM is negative; so it's closer to other clusters than its own (technically)
```
